entries.text: The MessagePackAnalyzer NuGet package provides compiler warnings, code fixes, and optional AOT formatter generation.
Users who want Json.NET-like behavior without attributes can use the ContractlessStandardResolver.
If all keys are integer indexes the object serializes as a MessagePack array, otherwise as a map with string keys.
Gaps in integer key sequences are filled with null placeholders in the array, and indexes of removed members should not be reused.
MsgPack003, 004, 005, 006, 007, 008, 009, 011, 012, 016 and 018 are Errors, while MsgPack010, 013, 014, 015 and 017 are Warnings.
MsgPack004 requires public members of [MessagePackObject] types to have either [Key] or [IgnoreMember].
MsgPack001 and MsgPack002 are Disabled by default in the rule table.
Missing keys during deserialization leave members at their default value, so reference-type members can be null.
Requiring the MessagePackObject annotation by default is intentional, to enforce explicitness.
MsgPack017 warns that an init property initializer's default is replaced by the type's default value on deserialization.
Source generated formatters do not support everything dynamic formatters do, which is why MsgPack008 and MsgPack016 exist.

Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect.
Recent fixes to serializing BigInteger, Decimal, long numbers, and float SIMD show numeric serialization is bug-prone.
Source generator and TypeCollector logic has had many recent fixes, including name collisions, nested types, generic constraints, and recursive constraints that caused a stack overflow.
Analyzer diagnostics such as MsgPack003 and MsgPack004 have recently been adjusted for false positives, so changes can cause wrong reports.
